description: Calculates the 2025-2028 federal deduction for qualified overtime pay under the One Big Beautiful Bill Act (P.L. 119-21, IRC 225) as IRS Schedule 1-A Part III does: the $12,500 cap ($25,000 joint), then $100 off per full $1,000 of MAGI over $150,000 ($300,000 joint). Only the FLSA half-time premium qualifies, so it converts hourly rate, overtime hours and multiplier (or total overtime pay) to the qualified amount; double time does not double it. Married filing separately gets $0. Figures copied from irs.gov in Oct 2026.

filing_status.description: Federal filing status. married_filing_separately cannot claim these deductions.

hourly_rate.description: FLSA regular rate of pay per hour, in USD.

magi.description: Modified adjusted gross income in USD: Form 1040 line 11b plus excluded Puerto Rico and foreign income (Schedule 1-A Part I).

multiplier.description: Overtime pay multiplier. 1.5 = time-and-a-half (default), 2 = double time.

overtime_hours.description: Overtime hours over 40 in a workweek, summed for the year.

qualified_overtime_premium.description: Qualified overtime compensation already known, e.g. Form W-2 box 12 code TT. Use this OR the hourly fields OR total_overtime_pay.

tax_year.description: Tax year, 2025 to 2028. The deductions end after 2028.

total_overtime_pay.description: Total pay for the overtime hours (straight time plus premium).

name: calculate_overtime_deduction
title: No Tax on Overtime deduction
